domain: Deals, contracts, deliverables, shipments, disputes & reviews (47 endpoints)
graphify_note: graphify-out/ in the RC snapshot contains only cache/stat-index.json — graph.json does NOT exist in this checkout (confirmed: `graphify query` errored 'graph file not found'). All tracing below was done by direct source reading of the RC tree, per the audit rules' own fallback ('confirm in source').

questions.q: Is DealService the sole authorization point for accept/reject/counter/createProposal, and is that a risk given DealController carries no @PreAuthorize/@Secured?
questions.a: Confirmed by the code's own javadoc (DealService.java:243-248): DealController has zero method-level security annotations; every gate (role, brand membership tier, ownership) lives inside DealService. This is a single point of truth, not obviously wrong, but it means any new controller method that forgets to route through the same helper (requireOwnedCollaboration/requireBrandDealManagerWorkspace) has no second line of defense. All four flows were exercised by DealServiceTest (71/71 passing) and DealControllerTest (15/15 passing) in this pass.

questions.q: Is the shipment feature (address/create/confirm-receipt/get) tested before go-live?
questions.a: No. No ShipmentServiceTest file exists anywhere in influora-api/src/test (confirmed by `mvn -Dtest=ShipmentServiceTest` reporting 'No tests matching pattern'), and DealControllerTest only mocks ShipmentService as a constructor dependency — no test ever calls submitShippingAddress/markShipped/confirmReceipt/getShipment. The code itself (ShipmentService.java) reads as correct and defensive (unique-constraint race guard, IDOR-safe lookup-by-collaboration-not-by-shipment-id, http/https scheme allowlist on trackingUrl per a documented Kabir CRITICAL finding), but is IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED, not WORKING, by this audit's own evidence rules.

questions.q: Can a contract be cancelled and signed concurrently, producing an inconsistent state?
questions.a: Yes, this is a real, code-acknowledged gap. ContractService.cancel()/cancelForCreator() (ContractService.java:1029-1044) do NOT take a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock before check-then-write, unlike doRecordSignature (which does lock, specifically to close the analogous CR-22a race) and unlike DealService#doReject (which also locks). The class's own javadoc (lines 1017-1027) states this is a known, deliberately out-of-scope limitation. No test in ContractCancelAmendTest exercises the race.

questions.q: Is contract cancel/amend reachable from the frontend?
questions.a: No FE caller exists in either src/lib/api.ts or src/lib/meera-api.ts for POST /contracts/:id/cancel or /contracts/:id/amend (confirmed by grep across both files — zero matches). This matches the task's own annotation ('NO FE CALLER, API-only') — a brand or creator has no UI path to call off an unsigned/half-signed contract.

questions.q: Does the brand-side dispute list (BrandDisputeController -> DisputeService.listDisplayForBrand) have the same test rigor as the creator side?
questions.a: No. DisputeServiceTest has explicit happy-path AND tenant-isolation tests for listDisplayForCreator (lines 690-750) but zero tests for listDisplayForBrand, despite both methods sharing the same buildDisputeDisplayRows(...) row-mapping helper over structurally similar but distinct native/JPQL queries (findWithCollaborationByWorkspaceId vs. findWithCollaborationByCreatorUserId).

questions.q: Is GET /creator/disputes/eligible-deals guaranteed to show every deal a creator could actually open a dispute against?
questions.a: Not necessarily. DealService.listEligibleForDispute filters on DealResponse.escrowFunded, which (per DealService.java:2140-2157) is scoped to the collaboration's LATEST contract version's milestone once a contract exists. DisputeService.openDispute's own gate, EscrowService.hasFundedUnreleasedEscrow, is collaboration-wide across ALL contract versions. After a ContractService#amend, a FUNDED hold can be left bound to a superseded (non-latest) milestone — the exact scenario DealService's own comment calls out as a historical bug class in the other direction. Here it would make a genuinely fundable/disputable deal silently disappear from the picker, even though POST /deals/{id}/disputes would still 201 if reached another way. listEligibleForDispute has ZERO test coverage anywhere in the test tree, so this mismatch is unverified but plausible from direct code comparison (E2, moderate confidence).

questions.q: Do BrandReviewController / CreatorReviewController / BrandDisputeController / CreatorDisputeController have controller-level tests?
questions.a: No dedicated controller test file exists for any of the four (confirmed by filesystem search). Their handler bodies are one-line delegations to already well-tested services (ReviewService: 15/15 passing; DisputeService: 19/19 passing), so the residual risk is narrow — a routing/verb/annotation regression, not a logic bug — but it is genuinely unverified at the web layer, unlike DealController/ContractController/BrandDeliverableController/CreatorDeliverableController which all have their own controller tests.

questions.q: Is the realtime deal-message SSE stream (GET /deals/{dealId}/messages/stream) production-ready?
questions.a: Yes, with high confidence relative to the rest of this audit. It is unusually heavily documented (CR-31, CR-08, F-0442, F-0551, F-0667 all cited inline) and has both a backend test (DealMessageStreamRegistryTest) and a frontend vitest suite (src/lib/__tests__/deal-message-stream.test.ts) that this pass executed live: 10/10 passing, including the CR-31 clean-close-triggers-reconnect regression test. Authorization runs before the SseEmitter is created (DealController.java:146), reusing the exact same ownership check as listMessages/sendMessage.

questions.q: Are the DeliverableCleanupJob's two scheduled sweeps (cleanupSupersededRevisions, cleanupAbandonedDrafts) safe to run unattended?
questions.a: Both exist, are separately cron-scheduled, and DeliverableCleanupJobTest exists in the test tree — treated as OBSERVED/covered rather than a gap; full transactional/idempotency tracing of both sweeps was out of this pass's time budget and is flagged for a follow-up pass rather than asserted either way.

questions.q: Does the brand deliverable reject endpoint (BrandDeliverableController.reject, the 'B6' fix) have controller-level test coverage matching its service-level coverage?
questions.a: No. BrandDeliverableServiceTest covers reject extensively (testRejectSubmitted, testRejectMissingFeedback, testRejectInvalidState, testRejectForeignDeliverable), but BrandDeliverableControllerTest only exercises approve/revise/getDetail/getSafetyReview — reject's own controller wiring (route, request body binding) is untested at that layer.

questions.q: Were any of the claims above verified at runtime in this pass, or is this a pure code-reading audit?
questions.a: Both. mvn -Dtest was run against DealServiceTest (71 passing), DisputeServiceTest (19 passing), BrandDeliverableServiceTest (32), CreatorDeliverableServiceTest (62), ContractServiceTest (39), ContractCancelAmendTest (15), ReviewServiceTest (15), DealControllerTest (15), ContractControllerTest (4), BrandDeliverableControllerTest (4), CreatorDeliverableControllerTest (6) — all green, 0 failures/errors, read directly from target/surefire-reports/*.txt (not piped through grep, to avoid the known 'piped mvn hides BUILD FAILURE' trap). `npx vitest run src/lib/__tests__/deal-message-stream.test.ts` was run and passed 10/10. `mvn -Dtest=ShipmentServiceTest` was run specifically to confirm the file does not exist (it reported no matching tests). These runtime results raise the corresponding features from IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED to WORKING per this audit's evidence rules.

features.name: Deal lifecycle: list / get / create / accept / reject / counter

features.entry_point: DealController.java:65-112 (GET /deals, GET /deals/{id}, POST /deals, POST /deals/{id}/accept, POST /deals/{id}/reject, POST /deals/{id}/counter)
features.flow: FE src/pages/brand-deals.tsx / creator equivalents -> src/lib/api.ts deals.{list,get,create,accept,reject,counter} (api.ts:2513-2573) -> DealController -> DealService.{list,get,createProposal,accept,reject,counter} -> CollaborationRepository/DealMessageRepository/CampaignRepository/CreatorProfileRepository -> Collaboration entity state machine -> DealResponse -> FE
features.api: GET /deals, GET /deals/{id}, POST /deals, POST /deals/{id}/accept, POST /deals/{id}/reject, POST /deals/{id}/counter
features.database: collaborations table (Collaboration entity: status, agreed_rate, usage_rights, campaign_id, creator_id); deal_messages (proposal/counter/system rows); reads campaigns, creator_profiles, workspaces
features.state_machine: IN_NEGOTIATION/INVITATION -> (counter*) -> TERMS_AGREED (accept) -> CONTRACT_PENDING (contract generated) -> ... ; reject/withdraw only allowed pre-contract (CR-22a narrowed Collaboration.canReject() to a pre-contract allowlist; CONTRACT_PENDING+ returns 409 DEAL_NOT_REJECTABLE, superseded by the separate two-party termination flow CR-22b, out of this domain's scope as listed)
features.authz: DealService is the SOLE authz point (DealController has no @PreAuthorize/@Secured) — requireRole, requireOwnedCollaboration (findByIdAndCreatorId / findByIdAndWorkspaceId), requireBrandDealManagerWorkspace (OWNER/ADMIN/MANAGER tier) gate createProposal; accept/reject/counter are dual-role (brand OR creator) scoped to the caller's own collaboration
features.working_condition: A brand with OWNER/ADMIN/MANAGER membership can propose a deal within campaign budget/collaborator-cap limits; either party can counter/accept/reject while status is pre-contract; accept/reject are idempotent via IdempotencyService keyed off Idempotency-Key header or a deterministic lifecycle key, with reject additionally taking a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE row lock (findByIdForUpdate) to close a documented lost-update race (Kabir finding #6) against a concurrent ContractService.generate/recordSignature
features.failure_conditions: 409 DEAL_NOT_REJECTABLE once CONTRACT_PENDING+; 409 COLLABORATION_EXISTS on duplicate propose (DB unique constraint backstop); budget/collaborator-cap/agreed-rate validation errors on createProposal/counter; concurrent reject/accept resolved via row lock + idempotency replay, not silent overwrite
features.security_conditions: IDOR closed via ownership-scoped finders on every path; VIEWER-tier brand members correctly blocked from create/accept/reject/counter (closes a prior self-contradiction where VIEWER could propose but not counter, per CR-37 followup note in code); reject no longer denylist-shaped so it cannot cancel an escrow-funded signed deal unilaterally (CR-22a)
features.tests: DealServiceTest — 71/71 passing (executed live in this pass); DealControllerTest — 15/15 passing (executed live); DealServiceBudgetTest, DealServiceCollaboratorCapVerificationTest, DealServiceCreatorDraftExclusionTest, DealServiceEscrowContractScopeTest, DealTrailCoverageTest also present covering budget/cap/draft-exclusion/escrow-scope/audit-trail edge cases (not re-run in this pass, evidence from prior committed suite)
features.production_conditions: Standard DB + JWT auth; no external service dependency for this flow itself
features.evidence: Read DealController.java:65-231, DealService.java:241-560 (createProposal/accept/reject/doReject/counter) directly; ran `mvn -Dtest=DealServiceTest,DealControllerTest test` against the RC checkout — surefire reports confirm 71/71 and 15/15 passing, 0 failures/errors

features.name: Deal-room messaging incl. SSE stream
features.purpose: Realtime chat timeline inside a deal room, backed by DealMessage rows and a live SSE push channel so both parties see new messages without polling.
features.flow: FE brand-chat.tsx/brand-messages.tsx/creator-chat.tsx -> src/lib/api.ts messages.{list,send,markRead,stream} (list/send/markRead ~api.ts:2652-2677; stream ~api.ts:2729-2820, a hand-rolled fetch+ReadableStream SSE client, NOT native EventSource, because EventSource cannot send an Authorization header) -> DealController -> DealService.{listMessages,sendMessage,markRead,authorizeMessageStream} + DealMessageStreamRegistry (in-memory emitter registry with Last-Event-ID replay buffer) -> DealMessage entity/table -> DealMessageResponse pushed as named SSE event 'deal-message'
features.database: deal_messages table (kind, sender_type, content, metadata JSON, read_by JSON)
features.state_machine: N/A (append-only timeline); stream connection states: connecting -> open -> reconnecting (exponential backoff+jitter) -> open, replaying missed events via Last-Event-ID against DealMessageStreamRegistry's time-bounded buffer
features.authn: JWT Bearer token read explicitly via http.getToken(role) for the raw fetch-based SSE call (bypasses the normal axios/fetch interceptor, so a dedicated 401-driven refresh-once path was added, per F-0667/F-0551 code comments)
features.authz: DealController.streamMessages calls dealService.authorizeMessageStream BEFORE creating/registering the SseEmitter — an unauthorized caller gets a normal 404/403 and no emitter is ever created (DealController.java:146, documented explicitly)
features.working_condition: Both roles can list/send/mark-read messages on their own deal; the stream authorizes first, sends a comment-only heartbeat frame to open cleanly, and reconnects with backoff+jitter on ANY disconnection (including a clean server close, per the CR-31 fix) rather than going silently deaf
features.failure_conditions: A gap longer than the server's replay-buffer retention window is unrecoverable via Last-Event-ID and falls back to onReconnect triggering a full refetch; unauthorized dealId returns 403/404 before any emitter exists
features.security_conditions: Token never rides in the URL/query string (a core requirement driving the fetch-based design over EventSource); authorization reuses the exact same ownership check as listMessages/sendMessage
features.tests: DealMessageStreamRegistryTest (backend); src/lib/__tests__/deal-message-stream.test.ts (frontend) — executed live in this pass: 10/10 passing including the CR-31 clean-close-reconnect regression test; DealControllerTest covers stream authorization/Last-Event-ID passthrough/unauthorized-rejection (3 of its 15 tests)
features.production_conditions: Depends on the reverse proxy (Caddy, per comments) not buffering the SSE response; this was not independently verified against the actual deployed proxy config in this source-only pass
features.evidence: Read DealController.java:114-169, api.ts:2680-2820 directly; ran the vitest suite live (10/10 passing) via `npx vitest run src/lib/__tests__/deal-message-stream.test.ts`

features.name: Shipments: address / mark-shipped / confirm-receipt / get

features.database: shipments table, UNIQUE(collaboration_id); reads campaigns/workspaces/creator_profiles for notification field derivation
features.state_machine: AWAITING_ADDRESS (synthetic, no row) -> ADDRESS_PROVIDED -> SHIPPED -> RECEIVED(GOOD) | DAMAGED; address is editable only in AWAITING_ADDRESS/ADDRESS_PROVIDED (requireNotShipped allowlist, ShipmentService.java:291-304)
features.authz: Every entrypoint resolves identity via CreatorContextService/BrandContextService then authorizes the Collaboration via the same ownership finders DealService uses (findByIdAndCreatorId/findByIdAndWorkspaceId); the Shipment row itself is NEVER looked up by its own client-supplied id, only via findByCollaborationId AFTER ownership passes — the IDOR guard is explicit in the class javadoc (ShipmentService.java:46-52)
features.working_condition: Creator submits/updates an address before shipping; brand marks shipped with carrier/tracking (trackingUrl is scheme-validated to http/https only); creator confirms receipt in good or damaged condition; GET returns a synthetic AWAITING_ADDRESS response when no row exists yet rather than 404
features.failure_conditions: 409 SHIPMENT_ALREADY_SHIPPED on address edit after shipping; 409 SHIPMENT_NO_ADDRESS if brand tries to ship with no address on file; 409 SHIPMENT_NOT_SHIPPED if creator confirms receipt before SHIPPED; a UNIQUE(collaboration_id) DataIntegrityViolationException race on first-submit is caught and retried as an update rather than surfaced as a 500
features.security_conditions: trackingUrl is scheme-allowlisted to http/https server-side (ShipmentService.java:180-185, 269-289) specifically because it is later rendered as a creator-facing href and embedded in notification payloads — a documented Kabir CRITICAL finding fix (javascript:/data: stored-XSS class, same family as the CampaignLinkService fix)
features.tests: NONE FOUND. No ShipmentServiceTest file exists in influora-api/src/test (confirmed via targeted `mvn -Dtest=ShipmentServiceTest` reporting 'No tests matching pattern'); DealControllerTest mocks ShipmentService only as a constructor dependency and never exercises submitShippingAddress/markShipped/confirmReceipt/getShipment
features.production_conditions: Depends on notification system (ShipmentCreatedEvent/ShipmentReceivedEvent) and on CreatorContextService/BrandContextService resolving correctly; no Docker/Testcontainers dependency beyond the standard DB
features.evidence: Read ShipmentService.java in full (423 lines); ran `mvn -Dtest=ShipmentServiceTest test` and confirmed 'No tests matching pattern "ShipmentServiceTest" were executed'; grepped DealControllerTest for shipment-related @Test methods and found none
known_issues: Entire feature (4 endpoints, a 5-state machine, an XSS-prevention gate, and a race-condition retry path) has zero automated test coverage at any layer — the code reads as correct and defensive on direct inspection, but nothing in CI would catch a regression here.
required_fixes: Add a ShipmentServiceTest covering: happy-path address->ship->confirm(good)->confirm(damaged) transitions; the UNIQUE-constraint race-retry branch; requireNotShipped's allowlist on every non-editable state; the trackingUrl scheme-validation rejection paths (javascript:, data:, malformed URI); and ownership/IDOR checks for both roles. Add DealControllerTest coverage for the 4 shipment routes themselves.

features.name: Contracts: create / list / unsigned / get / sign / pdf-download-url
features.purpose: Generate a legally-binding Contract from an agreed deal, let each party e-sign it independently, and mint a short-lived presigned download URL for the fully-executed PDF.
features.flow: FE brand-contracts.tsx -> src/lib/api.ts contracts.{generate,list,get,sign,listUnsigned,pdfDownloadUrl} (api.ts:3200-3350) -> ContractController -> ContractService -> ContractRepository/PaymentMilestoneRepository/Contract entity -> PDF generation service -> presigned URL -> FE
features.api: POST /contracts, GET /contracts, GET /contracts/unsigned, GET /contracts/{contractId}, POST /contracts/{contractId}/sign, GET /contracts/{contractId}/pdf-download-url
features.database: contracts table (status, brand_signed_at, creator_signed_at, workspace_id, expiration_date computed from latest milestone due date), payment_milestones
features.state_machine: DRAFT/PENDING_SIGNATURES -> (both signatures via Contract.advanceIfFullySigned()) -> ACTIVE -> COMPLETED; sign is per-role idempotent (already-signed-by-this-role short-circuits to a no-op replay)
features.authz: generate/amend are brand-only at OWNER/ADMIN/MANAGER membership tier (brandContext.requireBrandWorkspace + requireRole); sign/get/list/cancel/pdf-download-url branch by principal.getUserType() (CREATOR vs BRAND) and route to role-scoped service methods (recordSignatureForCreator vs recordSignature) — the signer role is ALWAYS derived from the authenticated principal, never from the request body (explicit Swapnil ruling documented at ContractController.java:94-111, closing a prior brand-can-sign-on-a-creators-behalf hole)
features.working_condition: Brand generates a contract with milestones; each party signs with their own typed full name (signerName, F-0292); once both signatures are recorded the contract auto-advances to ACTIVE and a PDF is generated; pdf-download-url 404s with CONTRACT_PDF_NOT_READY until both signed and PDF generation completed
features.failure_conditions: A genuinely NEW signature takes a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the Collaboration row and re-checks CANCELLED under that lock (CR-22a, closing a race against a concurrent DealService#doReject) — but an idempotent replay of an already-recorded signature deliberately skips this to avoid touching the collaboration at all (verified via verifyNoInteractions in ContractServiceTest)
features.security_conditions: Creators cannot self-attribute a signature as BRAND (role read from principal, not body); a brand cannot forge a creator's signature (recordSignatureForCreator is a fully separate, creator-authenticated path)
features.tests: ContractServiceTest — 39/39 passing (executed live); ContractControllerTest — 4/4 passing (executed live); ContractPdfServiceTest, ContractRepositoryUnsignedByCreatorTest, ContractServiceDeliverableMaterializationTest also present (not re-run, evidence from prior committed suite)
features.production_conditions: Requires the PDF-generation pipeline and presigned-URL storage (R2/S3-shaped) to be configured; contract PDF readiness gating depends on that pipeline completing before pdf-download-url returns 200
features.evidence: Read ContractController.java in full (168 lines) and ContractService.java:960-1058, 1083+ directly; ran `mvn -Dtest=ContractServiceTest,ContractControllerTest test` — 39/39 and 4/4 passing per surefire reports

features.name: Contract cancel / amend (API-only, no FE caller)
features.purpose: Cancel a not-yet-fully-executed contract (either party), or amend an ACTIVE contract's terms/milestones by generating a new versioned Contract row rather than mutating in place.
features.flow: No FE caller in src/lib/api.ts or src/lib/meera-api.ts (confirmed by grep, zero matches for contract cancel/amend in either file) -> ContractController.cancel/amend -> ContractService.cancel/cancelForCreator/amend -> Contract entity -> ContractRepository
features.database: contracts table (status -> CANCELLED, or a new versioned row for amend); milestones
features.state_machine: cancel: Contract.canCancel() admits only DRAFT/PENDING_SIGNATURES (ACTIVE deliberately excluded, mirroring the CR-22a lesson from Collaboration#canReject()) -> CANCELLED; amend: creates a new versioned Contract row and retires/cancels the predecessor rather than mutating history in place
features.authz: cancel is dual-role (brand at OWNER/ADMIN/MANAGER tier, or the creator themselves) mirroring DealService#reject's rationale; amend is brand-only at the same elevated tier as generate
features.working_condition: A brand or creator can cancel a DRAFT/PENDING_SIGNATURES contract; a brand can amend an ACTIVE contract into a new version
features.security_conditions: No new exposure found; role/tier checks mirror generate/sign
features.tests: ContractCancelAmendTest — 15/15 passing (executed live), covering DRAFT/PENDING_SIGNATURES/ACTIVE/COMPLETED/ALREADY_CANCELLED cancel transitions, creator-own-draft cancel, amend-creates-new-version, amend-cancels-predecessor, stale-version rejection, amend-on-cancelled/completed rejection, empty-milestones rejection, and total-exceeds-agreed-rate rejection — but NO concurrency test for cancel racing sign (see Finding on the missing row lock)
features.evidence: Read ContractController.java:117-151 and ContractService.java:987-1058 directly (including the class's own documented concurrency-scope-limitation note); grepped src/lib/api.ts and src/lib/meera-api.ts for 'cancel'/'amend' near 'contract' — zero results in either; confirmed via ContractCancelAmendTest test-name enumeration that no concurrency test exists
known_issues: No frontend caller anywhere in the two FE API layers — brand/creator have no UI path to cancel or amend a contract despite full backend support.

ContractService.cancel()/cancelForCreator() take no PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock before check-then-write, unlike doRecordSignature/DealService#doReject — a concurrent cancel and sign on the same contract is not fully race-safe. This is explicitly acknowledged in the method's own javadoc as an out-of-scope known limitation, not a new discovery.
required_fixes: Decide and, if needed, wire an FE entry point (brand-contracts.tsx and/or the creator contracts view) for cancel/amend, or explicitly document them as support/API-only by design.

Add ContractRepository.findByIdForUpdate (or equivalent) and take the same PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock in doCancel that doRecordSignature already takes, then add a concurrency test mirroring the existing CR-22a-style coverage.

features.failure_conditions: 409 on invalid-state transitions for every mutating action; markPosted rejects http (non-https), file:, javascript: schemes, localhost/loopback/private-range/cloud-metadata IPs, lookalike/path-spoofed hosts, and overlong/XSS-tail URLs — each with its own dedicated test
features.security_conditions: markPosted's URL validator is an SSRF+XSS hardening surface with 15+ dedicated rejection tests (host spoofing, cloud metadata IP 169.254.169.254-class, encoded script tags treated as opaque strings, etc.) — the single most heavily security-tested endpoint found in this domain
features.tests: CreatorDeliverableServiceTest — 62/62 passing (executed live); CreatorDeliverableControllerTest — 6/6 passing (executed live); CreatorDeliverableServiceManualFallbackTest also present (3 tests, not re-run)
features.production_conditions: File upload depends on R2/object storage configuration; verify depends on the Meta Graph API integration (DeliverableVerificationService) being configured with valid credentials
features.evidence: Read CreatorDeliverableController.java in full; ran `mvn -Dtest=CreatorDeliverableServiceTest,CreatorDeliverableControllerTest test` — 62/62 and 6/6 passing per surefire reports; enumerated the full markPosted-rejection test list (15 distinct URL-validation tests)

features.name: Disputes: raise / list / eligible-deals
features.purpose: Either party opens a dispute against a deal with funded, unreleased escrow; each side gets its own read-only, display-enriched dispute list; a creator gets a pre-filtered dropdown of deals eligible for a new dispute.
features.flow: FE brand-disputes.tsx / creator dispute UI -> src/lib/api.ts disputes.{open,listForBrand,listForCreator,eligibleDeals} (api.ts:6335-6452) -> DealController.openDispute / BrandDisputeController.listDisplay / CreatorDisputeController.{list,eligibleDeals} -> DisputeService / DealService.listEligibleForDispute -> DisputeRepository/CollaborationRepository/EscrowHoldRepository -> DealResponse/DisputeListItemResponse
features.database: disputes table (status, opener_type, reason), reads collaborations/campaigns/escrow_holds; opening a dispute also writes collaboration.status = DISPUTED and freezes escrow holds
features.state_machine: openDispute requires funded+unreleased escrow (409 NO_FUNDED_ESCROW otherwise) and no existing active dispute (409 DISPUTE_ALREADY_OPEN); freezes escrow BEFORE persisting the Dispute row (H-T34-1 ordering discipline, explicit in code) so a crash between the two steps can never leave a persisted OPEN dispute with unfrozen escrow
features.authz: openDispute resolves ownership via the same collaboration finders as DealService; listDisplayForBrand scopes via brandContext.requireBrandWorkspace + campaign.workspace_id join; listDisplayForCreator scopes via creatorContext.requireCreator
features.working_condition: Either party opens a dispute only against a deal with real, unreleased, funded escrow; brand and creator each see a display-enriched (campaign/counterparty name) list of their own disputes; a creator sees a filtered eligible-deals dropdown excluding DISPUTED/COMPLETED/CANCELLED collaborations and non-funded ones
features.security_conditions: listDisplayForCreator has an explicit tenant-isolation test proving a foreign creator's disputes never leak (DisputeServiceTest lines 720-750); listDisplayForBrand has NO equivalent test despite sharing the same row-building helper over a structurally similar but distinct query
features.tests: DisputeServiceTest — 19/19 passing (executed live), fully covering openDispute (happy path, wrong-deal/wrong-workspace IDOR rejection, already-disputed rejection, no-escrow rejection, freeze-before-save ordering) and listDisplayForCreator (happy path + tenant isolation) — but ZERO tests for listDisplayForBrand or for DealService.listEligibleForDispute (confirmed via grep: neither method name appears anywhere in influora-api/src/test)
features.production_conditions: Depends on EscrowService's freeze/hold primitives being correctly configured
features.evidence: Read DealController.java:185-193, BrandDisputeController.java, CreatorDisputeController.java, DisputeService.java:100-148,478-499, DealService.java:1469-1509 directly; ran `mvn -Dtest=DisputeServiceTest test` — 19/19 passing per surefire report; grepped the full test tree for 'listDisplayForBrand' and 'listEligibleForDispute' — zero matches for either
known_issues: DisputeService.listDisplayForBrand has zero test coverage while its creator-side sibling has explicit tenant-isolation coverage — an asymmetric gap over structurally similar native/JPQL queries.

DealService.listEligibleForDispute (backing the creator's 'open a dispute' deal picker) has zero test coverage anywhere, and its escrowFunded filter is scoped to the collaboration's LATEST contract version (per DealService.java:2140-2157's own comment about ContractService#amend leaving old FUNDED holds bound to superseded milestones), while DisputeService.openDispute's own gate (EscrowService.hasFundedUnreleasedEscrow) is collaboration-wide across ALL contract versions. After a contract amendment, a genuinely disputable deal (funded escrow on a superseded milestone) could be silently excluded from the eligible-deals picker even though POST /deals/{id}/disputes would still succeed if reached another way.
required_fixes: Add a listDisplayForBrand test mirroring the existing listDisplayForCreator happy-path + tenant-isolation coverage.

Add a listEligibleForDispute test, including a case with a FUNDED hold on a superseded (non-latest) contract milestone, to confirm whether the picker's scoping matches or diverges from openDispute's own escrow gate; if it diverges, either broaden escrowFunded's scope for this specific query or document the narrower picker semantics as intentional.

features.name: Two-way reviews: submit / received / flag
features.purpose: After a collaboration reaches COMPLETED, each party can leave a one-time star rating + text review of the other, view reviews received, and flag an inappropriate received review for moderation.
features.entry_point: BrandReviewController.java, CreatorReviewController.java (both full files, ~59 lines each)
features.flow: FE brand-reviews.tsx / creator reviews view -> src/lib/api.ts reviews.* (api.ts:5356-5400) -> Brand/CreatorReviewController -> ReviewService -> ReviewRepository/ContentFlagRepository -> CollaborationRepository (ownership + COMPLETED-status gate)
features.api: POST /brand/reviews, GET /brand/reviews/received, POST /brand/reviews/{reviewId}/flag, POST /creator/reviews, GET /creator/reviews/received, POST /creator/reviews/{reviewId}/flag
features.database: reviews table (UNIQUE per collaboration+reviewer_type, enforced by both an explicit existsBy check AND a DB unique-constraint catch), content_flags table (UNIQUE per content+flagged-by-user)
features.state_machine: Review creation gated strictly on Collaboration.status == COMPLETED (409 COLLABORATION_NOT_COMPLETED otherwise); one review per (collaboration, reviewer_type) — a second attempt is 409 ALREADY_REVIEWED whether caught by the pre-check or the DB constraint race; flagging is one-per-(review, flagger) — 409 ALREADY_FLAGGED on a repeat
features.authz: requireOwnedCollaboration scopes review creation to the caller's own collaboration by role; requireReviewForParty re-derives ownership from the Collaboration behind the review (not the Review row's own reviewer field) before allowing a flag, closing an IDOR where a party could otherwise flag any reviewId by number
features.working_condition: A party can leave exactly one review after COMPLETED, read reviews received about them, and flag a received review once with a non-blank reason
features.failure_conditions: 409 COLLABORATION_NOT_COMPLETED, 409 ALREADY_REVIEWED (both pre-check and DB-race paths), 400 INVALID_REQUEST on blank flag reason, 409 ALREADY_FLAGGED, 404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND when the review doesn't belong to the caller's own collaboration (IDOR-safe by returning NOT_FOUND rather than FORBIDDEN, avoiding existence leakage)
features.security_conditions: Flag-preview truncated to 200 chars before storage; requireReviewForParty's ownership re-derivation prevents a brand/creator from flagging a review on a collaboration that isn't theirs even if they guess a valid reviewId
features.tests: ReviewServiceTest — 15/15 passing (executed live). NO controller-level test exists for BrandReviewController or CreatorReviewController (confirmed by filesystem search) — both are thin one-line delegations, so residual risk is limited to routing/annotation wiring, not business logic
features.evidence: Read BrandReviewController.java, CreatorReviewController.java, ReviewService.java in full; ran `mvn -Dtest=ReviewServiceTest test` — 15/15 passing per surefire report; filesystem search confirmed no *ReviewControllerTest* files exist
known_issues: Zero controller-level tests for either review controller, unlike DealController/ContractController/BrandDeliverableController/CreatorDeliverableController which all have their own controller test files.
required_fixes: Add BrandReviewControllerTest and CreatorReviewControllerTest covering routing, auth-principal wiring, and the 201/200 status codes for create/list/flag.

features.name: Jobs: DeliverableVerificationJob, DeliverableCleanupJob (x2 sweeps)
features.purpose: DeliverableVerificationJob: every 6 hours, re-attempts platform (Meta) verification for every POSTED/METRICS_REPORTED deliverable with a live postUrl that isn't yet VERIFIED. DeliverableCleanupJob: two separate nightly sweeps — cleanupSupersededRevisions and cleanupAbandonedDrafts.
features.flow: Spring @Scheduled trigger -> ShedLock (@SchedulerLock, multi-instance-safe) -> in-memory AtomicBoolean overlap guard -> DeliverableRepository query -> per-item verification/cleanup with a defensive per-item try/catch so one failure never aborts the batch -> log.info tally
features.api: None (internal scheduled jobs, no HTTP surface)
features.database: deliverables table (status IN POSTED, METRICS_REPORTED for verification job; DeliverableCleanupJob's two sweeps target superseded-revision rows and abandoned-draft rows respectively, not fully traced in this pass)
features.state_machine: Verification job: POSTED/METRICS_REPORTED -> VERIFIED (via DeliverableVerificationService.verify), and once VERIFIED a deliverable is never revisited by this sweep
features.working_condition: DeliverableVerificationJob runs at most once per 6h window (ShedLock lockAtMostFor PT2H, lockAtLeastFor PT1M, plus a per-instance AtomicBoolean re-entrancy guard) and tallies outcomes without a single deliverable's failure aborting the sweep
features.failure_conditions: A per-deliverable exception is caught and logged, not propagated; ShedLock prevents two instances or two overlapping triggers from double-running
features.tests: DeliverableCleanupJobTest exists and covers the cleanup job. DeliverableVerificationServiceTest exists and covers the underlying verification logic the job calls, but no dedicated DeliverableVerificationJobTest was found exercising the job's own sweep/tally/overlap-guard behavior directly
features.production_conditions: Requires ShedLock's backing table/lock provider to be configured for multi-instance deployments; DeliverableVerificationJob depends on the Meta Graph API integration being reachable and credentialed
features.evidence: Read DeliverableVerificationJob.java in full (94 lines) and the @Scheduled/method signatures of DeliverableCleanupJob.java; confirmed DeliverableCleanupJobTest exists via filesystem search; did not find a dedicated *VerificationJob*Test file exercising the job class itself (only DeliverableVerificationServiceTest for the service it delegates to)
known_issues: DeliverableVerificationJob's own sweep/tally/AtomicBoolean re-entrancy-guard behavior has no dedicated job-level test (only the underlying DeliverableVerificationService is unit-tested); DeliverableCleanupJob's two distinct sweeps were not individually traced for correctness in this pass given the time budget across a 47-endpoint domain.
required_fixes: Add a DeliverableVerificationJobTest exercising the sweep against a mixed batch (some verify-success, some throw) to prove the per-item catch truly isolates failures and the tally is accurate.

findings.title: Shipment feature (4 endpoints, full state machine) has zero automated test coverage at any layer
findings.evidence: No ShipmentServiceTest file exists in influora-api/src/test (confirmed by running `mvn -o -Dtest=ShipmentServiceTest test`, which reported 'No tests matching pattern "ShipmentServiceTest" were executed'). DealControllerTest constructs DealController with a @Mock ShipmentService but no @Test method in that file ever calls submitShippingAddress/markShipped/confirmReceipt/getShipment.
findings.impact: A regression in address-lock enforcement, the XSS-preventing trackingUrl scheme gate, the UNIQUE-constraint race retry, or the IDOR-safe collaboration-scoped lookup would ship silently with no test to catch it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add ShipmentServiceTest covering the full state machine (AWAITING_ADDRESS->ADDRESS_PROVIDED->SHIPPED->RECEIVED/DAMAGED), the requireNotShipped allowlist, the trackingUrl scheme-validation rejections, the DataIntegrityViolationException race-retry branch, and ownership/IDOR checks for both roles; add the 4 corresponding controller-test cases.
findings.verification_required: Write and run the above tests against the current ShipmentService implementation; confirm they pass without modifying production code (the code reads correct on inspection — this is a coverage gap, not a known-broken feature).

findings.title: ContractService.cancel()/cancelForCreator() lack the row lock that the analogous sign/reject paths take, creating an unclosed concurrent cancel-vs-sign race
findings.evidence: ContractService.java:1017-1027's own javadoc states this explicitly as a known, deliberately out-of-scope limitation: 'this method does NOT take an equivalent row lock on the Contract row... A genuinely concurrent cancel racing a genuinely concurrent recordSignature/recordSignatureForCreator for the SAME contract is therefore not fully closed.' doRecordSignature (line ~1083) DOES take a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the Collaboration row for the equivalent CR-22a race. ContractCancelAmendTest's 15 tests cover every state-transition case but no concurrency scenario.
findings.impact: A brand/creator racing a cancel() against a concurrent sign (recordSignature/recordSignatureForCreator) on the same not-yet-fully-executed contract could, in principle, end up with an inconsistent outcome (e.g. a signature recorded on a contract simultaneously being cancelled) since neither side observes the other's in-flight write under a shared lock.
findings.recommended_fix: Add ContractRepository.findByIdForUpdate (mirroring CollaborationRepository's own) and take the same PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock in doCancel before the canCancel() check-then-write, then add a concurrency test analogous to the existing collaboration-level CR-22a coverage.
findings.verification_required: A concurrency/interleaving test (e.g. using two threads or an explicit lock-ordering test with a test double) demonstrating the current code allows both operations to commit, followed by re-running it after the fix to confirm one is serialized behind the other.

findings.title: DisputeService.listDisplayForBrand and DealService.listEligibleForDispute have zero test coverage; the latter's escrow-funded filter may diverge from openDispute's own gate after a contract amendment
findings.evidence: Grepped the entire test tree for 'listDisplayForBrand' and 'listEligibleForDispute' — zero matches for either, versus listDisplayForCreator's explicit happy-path + tenant-isolation tests (DisputeServiceTest.java:690-750). Read DealService.java:2140-2157: escrowFunded (used by listEligibleForDispute's filter) is scoped to the collaboration's LATEST contract version's milestone once a contract exists, per the code's own comment about ContractService#amend leaving old FUNDED holds bound to a superseded milestone. DisputeService.openDispute's gate, EscrowService.hasFundedUnreleasedEscrow (EscrowService.java:1203-1205), is collaboration-wide across all contract versions via findFundedHoldsForCollaboration.
findings.impact: After a contract amendment leaves a FUNDED hold on a superseded (non-latest) milestone, a genuinely dispute-eligible deal could be silently missing from the creator's 'open a dispute' picker (GET /creator/disputes/eligible-deals) even though the underlying POST /deals/{id}/disputes call would still succeed. Separately, an untested brand-side dispute list query carries the same class of silent-query-bug risk the creator side is explicitly guarded against by its tenant-isolation test.
findings.recommended_fix: Add listDisplayForBrand tests mirroring the creator-side happy-path + tenant-isolation coverage. Add a listEligibleForDispute test with a FUNDED hold on a superseded contract milestone to determine whether the divergence from openDispute's own gate is real; if real, either broaden escrowFunded's scope for this specific query or document the narrower semantics as intentional.
findings.verification_required: A test collaboration with an amended contract (predecessor + latest versions) where only the predecessor's milestone has a FUNDED hold: call listEligibleForDispute and confirm whether the deal is included, then call openDispute directly on that same deal and confirm whether it succeeds — a WORKING-eligible-list-excludes-it-but-openDispute-succeeds result would confirm the mismatch as a real, reproducible bug.

findings.title: Contract cancel/amend endpoints have no frontend caller in either FE API layer
findings.evidence: Grepped src/lib/api.ts and src/lib/meera-api.ts for 'cancel'/'amend' near contract routes — zero matches in either file for POST /contracts/:id/cancel or /contracts/:id/amend, despite both being fully implemented and well-tested (ContractCancelAmendTest, 15/15 passing) on the backend.
findings.location: src/lib/api.ts (no matching entry); src/lib/meera-api.ts (no matching entry); backend at ContractController.java:125,144
findings.impact: A brand or creator who wants to call off or amend a not-yet-fully-executed contract has no in-product path to do so — the only way to reach these endpoints today is a direct API call, which is not realistic for an end user. For go-live, this is a feature-completeness gap rather than a defect in what exists.
findings.recommended_fix: Either wire a cancel/amend action into brand-contracts.tsx (and the creator contract view) or explicitly confirm with product that this remains an admin/support-only, API-driven capability for this release.
findings.verification_required: Confirm with the product owner whether cancel/amend are intentionally excluded from this release's UI or a genuine gap to close before go-live.

findings.title: No controller-level tests for BrandReviewController, CreatorReviewController, BrandDisputeController, or CreatorDisputeController
findings.evidence: Filesystem search for *ReviewControllerTest* and *BrandDispute*/*CreatorDispute*Test* under influora-api/src/test returned no matches, in contrast to DealController/ContractController/BrandDeliverableController/CreatorDeliverableController which each have their own controller test file.
findings.impact: Low, since the underlying services are well-tested (ReviewServiceTest 15/15, DisputeServiceTest 19/19) and the controllers are one-line delegations, but a routing/HTTP-verb/@AuthenticationPrincipal wiring regression in any of these 4 controllers would not be caught by any existing automated test.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a thin MockMvc/unit controller test per class asserting the route, status code, and delegate call for each method.
findings.verification_required: N/A — this is a coverage gap, not a suspected defect; adding the tests is itself the verification.

findings.title: graphify-out/graph.json does not exist in the release-candidate snapshot despite CLAUDE.md mandating graphify query as the first step
findings.evidence: `graphify query "..."` from the RC directory returned: 'error: graph file not found: ...\rc-115f698\graphify-out\graph.json'. Directory listing of graphify-out/ in the RC checkout shows only cache/stat-index.json and cache/ast/ — no graph.json.
findings.impact: Not a product defect — a tooling/process note. This audit fell back to direct source reading per the task's own instruction ('you may run graphify query... to orient, then confirm in source'), so it did not block the assessment, but any future pass relying on graphify for this domain will hit the same wall until the graph is regenerated for this checkout.
findings.recommended_fix: Run `graphify update .` (or the equivalent full build) against this RC checkout/tag if graphify-backed audits of this exact commit are expected going forward.
findings.verification_required: None — directly reproduced by running the command.
